instruction: QA rule: template literals and script tags must close — never truncate output
input: An app's JS died with 'Unexpected end of input' because a backtick template literal was never closed. How do you avoid derailing?
output: 'Unexpected end of input' means the parser hit the end of the script inside an unclosed string/template/block. Guard rails: (1) every backtick ` opens AND closes a template — count them in pairs; (2) every <script> has a matching </script>; (3) every { has a matching }; (4) the file ends with </html>. If a section is too long, split it — never stop mid-string. One unclosed backtick kills the ENTIRE script.

instruction: QA rule: never create hundreds of thousands of objects — use InstancedMesh and few lights
input: An app built a city with nested loops over a 1000x1000 grid creating ~110k Box meshes and ~200k PointLights, then the browser tab crashed. What is the right approach?
output: Per-object Meshes and especially PointLights are expensive: a scene with 100k+ objects or thousands of lights will freeze or crash the GPU/software renderer. For repeated geometry use ONE InstancedMesh with per-instance transforms (setMatrixAt), and light the whole scene with 1-3 lights (ambient + a sun/directional or spotlight). Never add a light inside a build loop.
